message.content:
In Texas, tenants have a number of statutory rights designed to protect them from unfair treatment and to ensure they receive a safe, habitable living environment. Below is an overview of key rights you should know: | Category | What It Means | Practical Tips | |----------|---------------|----------------| | **Security Deposit** | Landlords may collect a security deposit but cannot charge more than one month’s rent (unless the lease specifies otherwise). | Keep a copy of the lease and any receipts. Ask for a written itemized list of deductions if you’re asked to pay extra. | | **Habitability** | The landlord must keep the property in a livable condition—plumbing, heating, electrical, structural safety, pest control, etc. | Document any problems with photos or videos. Send written notices to the landlord and keep copies. | | **Repair & Maintenance** | If the landlord fails to fix major issues, you can:
• Request repairs in writing.
• Pay for repairs yourself and deduct the cost from your rent (only if the landlord is in default).
• Withhold rent (in some cases) or terminate the lease. | Keep receipts for any repairs you pay for. | | **Rent Payment** | Rent is due on the date specified in the lease. Late fees are allowed only if the lease states them. | Pay on time or in writing. If you’re late, ask for a grace period. | | **Notice Requirements** | • For non‑payment: 3 days’ notice to pay or vacate.
• For lease termination: 30 days’ notice for month‑to‑month agreements.
• For eviction: 3 days’ notice to cure or quit. | Use certified mail or a reliable delivery service to prove notice was sent. | | **Privacy** | Landlords must give reasonable notice (usually 24 hours) before entering the unit, except in emergencies. | Keep a log of all entries. | | **Discrimination** | Under federal Fair Housing Act and Texas law, landlords cannot discriminate based on race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability, familial status, or other protected classes. | Report discrimination to the Texas Commission on Human Rights or the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development. | | **Lease Terms** | The lease must be in writing and signed by both parties. | Read the lease carefully before signing. | | **Eviction Process** | Landlords must follow the legal eviction process: serve notice, file a lawsuit, obtain a judgment, and then have a sheriff execute the eviction. | If you receive an eviction notice, respond promptly and consider seeking legal advice. | | **Retaliation** | Landlords cannot retaliate against tenants who exercise their rights (e.g., filing a complaint, requesting repairs). | Keep records of any retaliatory actions. | | **Right to a Written Lease** | Even if you’re on a month‑to‑month agreement, you can request a written lease. | A written lease clarifies responsibilities and protects both parties. | ### How to Protect Your Rights 1. **Document Everything** – Keep copies of leases, notices, repair requests, and any communication with your landlord. 2. **Know the Law** – Familiarize yourself with the Texas Property Code (especially Chapters 92–94). 3. **Use Certified Mail** – When sending notices, use certified or registered mail to have proof of delivery. 4. **Seek Legal Help** – If you’re facing eviction or a dispute, consult a tenant‑rights organization or attorney. 5. **Report Problems** – If the landlord fails to address habitability issues, you can file a complaint with the Texas Commission on Human Rights or the local housing authority. ### Resources - **Texas Property Code** – Chapter 92 (Residential Landlord‑Tenant Law). - **Texas Commission on Human Rights** – [https://www.tchra.texas.gov](https://www.tchra.texas.gov) - **Local Tenant‑Rights Groups** – Many cities have nonprofit organizations that offer free or low‑cost legal assistance. - **Legal Aid** – Check for local legal aid offices that specialize in housing law. If you have a specific situation (e.g., a notice you received, a repair issue, or a dispute over a security deposit), feel free to share more details so I can give more tailored guidance.
